inScope: Allow a public visitor to submit initial adoption interest from an animal profile for later staff handling.
Define an incremental proposal for an adoption-interest boundary without implementing the complete adoption process.
outOfScope: Applicant screening, authentication, automatic approval, and the complete adoption process.
Public exposure of applicant data in animal-profile responses.

assumptions: Applicant fields, consent wording, retention period, duplicate-interest handling, and privacy review remain unresolved validation work.
Later staff handling is a required concern, but no staff workflow is proposed as implemented functionality.
An explicit status-transition policy may be needed if interest registration will later affect Animal status; no current transition policy is established.

alternatives.description: Keep the current public profile link as a future placeholder and defer interest data capture until the broader adoption prototype.
alternatives.consequence: This has minimal immediate domain and privacy impact, but does not satisfy the concern of allowing visitors to register initial interest now.

alternatives.description: Add a narrowly scoped public adoption-interest submission use case associated with an Animal, persisting applicant data behind a non-public boundary for later staff handling.
alternatives.consequence: This enables initial interest registration while keeping screening, authentication, staff-review implementation, and the complete adoption process out of scope. It requires validation of privacy, consent, retention, and duplicate policy.

alternatives.description: Reuse the existing Animal status update capability to mark an animal as being in an adoption process whenever a visitor submits interest.
alternatives.consequence: This would require an explicit status-transition policy because current domain code does not encode permitted transitions. It also risks treating an unreviewed interest as a business-state change without supplied evidence that this is desired.

selectedOption.rationale: A dedicated, minimal interest-registration use case addresses the requested visitor interaction while preserving the established separation between interface, application, domain, and infrastructure. It can keep applicant information outside public animal-profile responses and defer unresolved policy decisions and later staff workflow implementation.

webContext.interactionFlow: From a public animal detail page, replace or evolve the current future-interest link into a submission interaction that sends initial interest for the identified animal. The submission is retained for later staff handling; screening, authentication, automatic approval, and staff-review implementation remain outside this increment.
boundaries: The public animal detail page currently contains a future-interest link and no implemented interest form.
The current Animals API has no adoption-interest endpoint.
Applicant data, if introduced, must remain outside public animal-profile responses.
Interface, application, domain, and infrastructure responsibilities should remain separated.
webContext.dataVisibility: Public animal-profile responses must not return applicant data. Any retained interest data should be available only through a future non-public staff-handling concern, whose concrete access mechanism is not established by the supplied evidence.
qualityAttributes: Privacy is a validation concern because consent, retention, duplicate-interest policy, and privacy checks are unresolved.
Traceability requires documenting relevant architectural changes with versioned ADRs, diagrams, and reusable prompts.

domainRules.rule: Initial interest should be associated with a specific Animal as a future-planned AdoptionInterest-related concept; the exact model and fields require design validation.
The proposal uses AVAILABLE as the eligible Animal status for accepting initial interest, subject to validation that this is the intended business policy.

Submitting initial interest does not itself establish a change from AVAILABLE to another Animal status in this proposal. Any future state change requires an explicit transition policy because permitted transitions are not currently encoded.
Applicant information must not be included in public animal-profile responses.

validation: Define consent requirements and applicant-data privacy checks before retaining submitted interest.
Define applicant-data retention and deletion policy.
Define duplicate-interest policy, including whether repeated submissions for the same animal and applicant are accepted, merged, or rejected.
Validate the minimum applicant fields needed for later staff handling.
Validate whether only AVAILABLE animals can accept interest and, if status changes are later introduced, define explicit permitted Animal status transitions.
Validate the non-public access boundary for future staff handling without implementing staff review in this increment.
documentationUpdates: Create a versioned ADR describing the initial adoption-interest boundary, public-data visibility restriction, use of AVAILABLE, and deferred transition-policy decision.
Update the domain diagram to show the planned AdoptionInterest relationship to Animal and the non-public applicant-data boundary.
Update reusable prompts to reflect the documented decision and unresolved policy validations.
Update functional scope documentation if initial interest registration is added to the delivered increment.
Update architecture documentation if the new application, domain, or infrastructure boundary changes the described structure.
